content.user_title: Build Molecular ML Workflows with DeepChem
content.value_statement: Molecular machine learning requires specialized data handling, featurization, splitting, and model selection. This skill provides DeepChem guidance, reference workflows, and runnable training scripts.
actual_capabilities: Recommends DeepChem loaders and featurizers for molecular structures, sequences, fingerprints, descriptors, and graph inputs.
Explains scaffold-based splitting, normalization, class balancing, and evaluation practices for molecular datasets.
Provides scripts for solubility prediction, graph neural network training, and pretrained model fine-tuning.
Covers MoleculeNet datasets for classification, regression, quantum properties, binding, and materials research.
Guides model selection across traditional machine learning, dense networks, graph models, and transfer learning.
Documents metrics, hyperparameter optimization, prediction workflows, molecular generation, and custom model integration.
limitations: Users must install DeepChem and the required model framework dependencies.
Some examples can require changes for the installed DeepChem version or dataset schema.
Benchmark datasets and pretrained models can require network downloads, disk space, memory, and substantial compute.
Model outputs require scientific validation and should not replace laboratory testing or clinical judgment.

use_cases.title: Plan a Molecular Property Study
use_cases.description: Select data loaders, featurizers, splits, models, and metrics for solubility, toxicity, activity, or ADMET prediction.

use_cases.title: Build a Graph Model Baseline
use_cases.description: Compare GCN, GAT, AttentiveFP, MPNN, and fingerprint baselines on a MoleculeNet or custom dataset.

use_cases.title: Adapt Pretrained Molecular Models
use_cases.description: Prepare scaffold splits and fine-tuning settings for ChemBERTa or GROVER on a small labeled dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Featurizer
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a DeepChem featurizer for [data type], [dataset size], and [model family]. Explain the choice, required inputs, and one suitable baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Training Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DeepChem workflow for predicting [property] from [input format]. Include loading, scaffold splitting, transformations, model selection, metrics, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Molecular Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [model A] and [model B] for [task] using [dataset]. Address featurization, sample size, compute, leakage risk, metrics, and expected tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced model selection and experiment design

prompt_templates.title: Plan Transfer Learning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a transfer learning plan for [pretrained model] on [custom dataset]. Specify data preparation, split strategy, fine-tuning settings, evaluation, failure checks, and reproducibility controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced adaptation of pretrained molecular models

output_examples.input: Recommend a workflow for predicting aqueous solubility from 2,500 labeled SMILES strings.
output: Representation: circular fingerprints provide a strong, efficient baseline for this dataset size.
Split: use molecular scaffolds to measure generalization to structurally distinct compounds.
Model: compare a random forest with a regularized multitask regressor.
Evaluation: report R2, mean absolute error, and root mean squared error on untouched test data.

output_examples.input: Compare GCN and AttentiveFP for a custom molecular classification dataset.
output: Both models require graph featurization and benefit from enough labeled molecules.
GCN offers a simpler baseline with lower tuning complexity.
AttentiveFP can model atom-level importance but may require more tuning and compute.
Use scaffold splits and report ROC-AUC with a metric suited to class imbalance.

output_examples.input: Plan ChemBERTa fine-tuning for a small blood-brain barrier dataset.
output: Preserve raw SMILES and divide compounds with a scaffold-based split.
Start with a low learning rate, few epochs, and validation-based stopping.
Compare against a fingerprint baseline to confirm that transfer learning adds value.
Record the model identifier, package versions, random seeds, and test metrics.

best_practices: Use scaffold-based splits for molecular prediction unless the scientific question requires another split.
Start with a fingerprint baseline before investing in graph networks or pretrained models.
Keep test data untouched and record data versions, transformations, seeds, metrics, and model settings.
anti_patterns: Do not use random molecular splits when structural similarity can leak across datasets.
Do not choose graph neural networks only because they are more complex.
Do not treat benchmark or model predictions as experimentally validated scientific conclusions.

faq.question: What data formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers CSV, SDF, FASTA, sequence alignment formats, arrays, images, and materials data through documented DeepChem loaders.

faq.question: Does the skill install DeepChem?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation commands, but users manage Python environments and optional framework dependencies.

faq.question: Can it work with custom molecular datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples accept custom CSV paths, SMILES columns, target columns, task types, and training settings.

faq.question: Which graph models are included?
faq.answer: The guidance covers GCN, GAT, AttentiveFP, MPNN, DMPNN, GROVER, and other models listed in the reference.

faq.question: Does it support pretrained models?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes ChemBERTa, GROVER, MolFormer, ProtBERT, and DeepChem wrappers for pretrained model workflows.

faq.question: Are predictions ready for laboratory or clinical use?
faq.answer: No. Predictions need domain review, uncertainty analysis, external validation, and experimental confirmation.
